notes: The UK government says it is illegal to import, sell, manufacture or drink alcohol in Iran, and that importing pork products is illegal.
The UK government says you need permission from the Iranian authorities to import or use drones or satellite phones; using them without permission is illegal and can lead to arrest.

Canada's travel advice says travellers have been denied entry because their passports bore an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing on the border with Israel.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Iran's economy is exclusively cash-based: credit cards are not accepted and ATMs serve only local bank accounts. The UK government adds that non-Iranian debit cards will not work, that changing money on the street is illegal, and that euros and US dollars are more commonly accepted at exchange offices than pounds sterling.

safety.text: Several Western governments advise against all travel to Iran, citing the risk of arbitrary detention — particularly for dual nationals and journalists — alongside regional conflict. Ordinary crime is low and visitors are generally received warmly, but the political risk is real: check your government's advisory before deciding to go.

tips.text: The UK government says Islamic dress codes are strictly enforced: in public, women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and men should wear long trousers and long-sleeved shirts.

US, UK and Canadian citizens must travel on a pre-approved itinerary with a government-licensed guide and are fingerprinted on arrival. The visa cannot be issued until the Ministry of Foreign Affairs grants an authorization code, so book through a specialist operator well ahead.
Iran's MFA describes visa on arrival only at its international airports (such as Tehran IKA); it says nothing about land borders, so if you arrive overland get the eVisa approval first.

Australia's Smartraveller says Iran does not recognise dual nationality and that foreign and dual nationals are at high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest, without guaranteed consular access. Many governments advise dual nationals not to travel.

Bring your whole budget in cash. The UK government says non-Iranian debit cards will not work, changing money on the street is illegal, and exchange offices accept euros and US dollars more readily than pounds sterling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iran?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do, but it is straightforward: apply online at evisa.mfa.ir or, if arriving by air, obtain a visa on arrival at major airports. A growing list of countries — including Turkey, several Gulf and Asian states and much of the former Soviet space — enters visa-free. US, UK and Canadian citizens are the exception and need an embassy visa with a guided tour.

faq.question: Can Americans visit Iran?
faq.answer: Yes, but only on an organized, pre-approved itinerary with a licensed guide. The visa requires a Ministry of Foreign Affairs authorization code arranged through a tour operator, and applicants are fingerprinted on arrival. The same rules apply to UK and Canadian citizens. Note that the US government advises against all travel to Iran.

faq.question: Can I visit Iran if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: Evidence of travel to Israel — stamps, visas, or border-crossing stamps from Egyptian or Jordanian land borders with Israel — leads to refusal of an Iranian visa or entry. Israeli citizens are barred entirely.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Iran?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says the economy is exclusively cash-based, credit cards are not accepted and ATMs serve only local bank accounts; the UK government adds that non-Iranian debit cards will not work. Bring your budget in cash, preferably US dollars or euros.

faq.question: What is the dress code for women in Iran?
faq.answer: The UK government says Islamic dress codes are strictly enforced. In public places women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and may be asked to wear a chador at religious sites. It also reports that the authorities have arrested and detained women for not following the dress code, and that enforcement crackdowns can happen at any time.

faq.question: Is Iran safe to visit?
faq.answer: Many governments advise against all travel. Australia's Smartraveller says do not travel to Iran and that foreigners, including dual nationals, are at high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest; the UK government says British and British-Iranian dual nationals face a very high risk of arrest, detention and questioning. Weigh the advisories seriously and keep insurance and registration in order if you go.
